[§](https://docs.rs#foreign-key-create)Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = ForeignKey::create()
    .name("FK_character_font")
    .from(Char::Table, Char::FontId)
    .to(Font::Table, Font::Id)
    .on_delete(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
    .on_update(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"ALTER TABLE `character`"#,
        r#"ADD CONSTRAINT `FK_character_font`"#,
        r#"FOREIGN KEY (`font_id`) REFERENCES `font` (`id`)"#,
        r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"ALTER TABLE "character" ADD CONSTRAINT "FK_character_font""#,
        r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id")"#,
        r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```

- Error types used in sea-query.

- Foreign key definition & alternations statements.

- For calling built-in SQL functions.
- [index](https://docs.rs/index/index.html)
- Index definition & alternations statements.
- [prepare](https://docs.rs/prepare/index.html)
- Helper for preparing SQL statements.
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- Query statements (select, insert, update & delete).
- [raw_sql](https://docs.rs/raw_sql/index.html)
- [schema](https://docs.rs/schema/index.html)

- Table definition & alternations statements.

- Base types used throughout sea-query.
- [value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html)
- Container for all SQL value types.

# sea_query - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sea-query/1.0.1/sea_query/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#seaquery)SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust.
You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API.
We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.
MS SQL Server Support is available under [SeaORM X](https://www.sea-ql.org/SeaORM-X/).

SeaQuery is written in 100% safe Rust. All workspace crates has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.
We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

[§](https://docs.rs#install)Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[dependencies]
sea-query = "1.0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional.

[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

Macro: `derive`

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`, `postgres-vector`

[§](https://docs.rs#motivation)Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

[§](https://docs.rs#1-parameter-bindings)1. Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can inject parameters right alongside the expression, and the $N sequencing will be handled for you. No more “off by one” errors!

```
assert_eq!(
    Query::select()
        .expr(Expr::col("size_w").add(1).mul(2))
        .from("glyph")
        .and_where(Expr::col("image").like("A"))
        .and_where(Expr::col("id").is_in([3, 4, 5]))
        .build(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    (
        r#"SELECT ("size_w" + $1) * $2 FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE $3 AND "id" IN ($4, $5, $6)"#
            .to_owned(),
        Values(vec![
            1.into(),
            2.into(),
            "A".to_owned().into(),
            3.into(),
            4.into(),
            5.into(),
        ])
    )
);
```
If you need an “escape hatch” to construct complex queries, you can use custom expressions, and still have the benefit of sequentially-binded parameters.

```
assert_eq!(
    Query::select()
        .columns(["size_w", "size_h"])
        .from("character")
        .and_where(Expr::col("id").eq(1)) // this is $1
        // custom expressions only need to define local parameter sequence.
        // its global sequence will be re-written.
        // here, we flip the order of $2 & $1 to make it look tricker!
        .and_where(Expr::cust_with_values(r#""size_w" = $2 * $1"#, [3, 2]))
        .and_where(Expr::col("size_h").gt(4)) // this is $N?
        .build(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    (
        r#"SELECT "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "id" = $1 AND ("size_w" = $2 * $3) AND "size_h" > $4"#
            .to_owned(),
        Values(vec![1.into(), 2.into(), 3.into(), 4.into()])
    )
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#2-dynamic-query)2. Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs with a fluent interface,
so you don’t have to append `WHERE` or `AND` conditionally.

```
fn query(a: Option<i32>, b: Option<char>) -> SelectStatement {
    Query::select()
        .column("id")
        .from("character")
        .apply_if(a, |q, v| {
            q.and_where(Expr::col("font_id").eq(v));
        })
        .apply_if(b, |q, v| {
            q.and_where(Expr::col("ascii").like(v));
        })
        .take()
}
assert_eq!(
    query(Some(5), Some('A')).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    "SELECT `id` FROM `character` WHERE `font_id` = 5 AND `ascii` LIKE 'A'"
);
assert_eq!(
    query(Some(5), None).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    "SELECT `id` FROM `character` WHERE `font_id` = 5"
);
assert_eq!(
    query(None, None).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    "SELECT `id` FROM `character`"
);
```
Conditions can be arbitrarily complex, thanks to SeaQuery’s internal AST:

```
assert_eq!(
    Query::select()
        .column("id")
        .from("glyph")
        .cond_where(
            Cond::any()
                .add(
                    Cond::all()
                        .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_null())
                        .add(Expr::col("image").is_null())
                )
                .add(
                    Cond::all()
                        .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_in([3, 4]))
                        .add(Expr::col("image").like("A%"))
                )
        )
        .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"SELECT "id" FROM "glyph""#,
        r#"WHERE"#,
        r#"("aspect" IS NULL AND "image" IS NULL)"#,
        r#"OR"#,
        r#"("aspect" IN (3, 4) AND "image" LIKE 'A%')"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
```
There is no superfluous parentheses `((((` cluttering the query, because SeaQuery respects
operator precedence when injecting them.

[§](https://docs.rs#3-cross-database-support)3. Cross database support

With SeaQuery, you can target multiple database backends while maintaining a single source of query logic.

```
let query = Query::insert()
    .into_table("glyph")
    .columns(["aspect", "image"])
    .values_panic([
        2.into(),
        3.into(),
    ])
    .on_conflict(
        OnConflict::column("id")
            .update_columns(["aspect", "image"])
            .to_owned(),
    )
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO `glyph` (`aspect`, `image`) VALUES (2, 3) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE `aspect` = VALUES(`aspect`), `image` = VALUES(`image`)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (2, 3) ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE SET "aspect" = "excluded"."aspect", "image" = "excluded"."image""#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (2, 3) ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE SET "aspect" = "excluded"."aspect", "image" = "excluded"."image""#
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#4-improved-raw-sql-ergonomics)4. Improved raw SQL ergonomics

SeaQuery 1.0 added a new `raw_query!` macro with named parameters, nested field access, array expansion and tuple expansion.
It surely will make crafting complex query easier.

```
let (a, b, c) = (1, 2, "A");
let d = vec![3, 4, 5];
let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
    PostgresQueryBuilder,
    r#"SELECT ("size_w" + {a}) * {b} FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE {c} AND "id" IN ({..d})"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.sql,
    r#"SELECT ("size_w" + $1) * $2 FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE $3 AND "id" IN ($4, $5, $6)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.values,
    Values(vec![
        1.into(),
        2.into(),
        "A".into(),
        3.into(),
        4.into(),
        5.into()
    ])
);
```
Insert with vector-of-tuple expansion.

```
let values = vec![(2.1345, "24B"), (5.15, "12A")];
let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
    PostgresQueryBuilder,
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES {..(values.0:1),}"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.sql,
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES ($1, $2), ($3, $4)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.values,
    Values(vec![2.1345.into(), "24B".into(), 5.15.into(), "12A".into()])
);
```
Update with nested field access.

```
struct Character {
    id: i32,
    font_size: u16,
}
let c = Character {
    id: 11,
    font_size: 22,
};
let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
    MysqlQueryBuilder,
    "UPDATE `character` SET `font_size` = {c.font_size} WHERE `id` = {c.id}"
);
assert_eq!(
    query.sql,
    "UPDATE `character` SET `font_size` = ? WHERE `id` = ?"
);
assert_eq!(query.values, Values(vec![22u16.into(), 11i32.into()]));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#basics)Basics

[§](https://docs.rs#iden)Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

You can use the `Iden` derive macro to implement it.

```
#[derive(Iden)]
enum Character {
    Table,
    Id,
    FontId,
    FontSize,
}
assert_eq!(Character::Table.to_string(), "character");
assert_eq!(Character::Id.to_string(), "id");
assert_eq!(Character::FontId.to_string(), "font_id");
assert_eq!(Character::FontSize.to_string(), "font_size");
#[derive(Iden)]
struct Glyph;
assert_eq!(Glyph.to_string(), "glyph");
```
```
use sea_query::{Iden, enum_def};
#[enum_def]
struct Character {
    pub foo: u64,
}
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
enum CharacterIden {
    Table,
    Foo,
}
assert_eq!(CharacterIden::Table.to_string(), "character");
assert_eq!(CharacterIden::Foo.to_string(), "foo");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#expression)Expression

Use [ Expr](https://docs.rs/expr/enum.Expr.html) constructors and

[methods to construct](https://docs.rs/expr/trait.ExprTrait.html)

`ExprTrait``SELECT`, `JOIN`, `WHERE` and `HAVING` expression in query.```
assert_eq!(
    Query::select()
        .column("char_code")
        .from("character")
        .and_where(
            Expr::col("size_w")
                .add(1)
                .mul(2)
                .eq(Expr::col("size_h").div(2).sub(1))
        )
        .and_where(
            Expr::col("size_w").in_subquery(
                Query::select()
                    .expr(Expr::cust_with_values("ln($1 ^ $2)", [2.4, 1.2]))
                    .take()
            )
        )
        .and_where(
            Expr::col("char_code")
                .like("D")
                .and(Expr::col("char_code").like("E"))
        )
        .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"SELECT "char_code" FROM "character""#,
        r#"WHERE ("size_w" + 1) * 2 = ("size_h" / 2) - 1"#,
        r#"AND "size_w" IN (SELECT ln(2.4 ^ 1.2))"#,
        r#"AND ("char_code" LIKE 'D' AND "char_code" LIKE 'E')"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#condition)Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [ Condition](https://docs.rs/query/struct.Condition.html) builder,
usable for

[and](https://docs.rs/query/trait.ConditionalStatement.html#tymethod.cond_where)

`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`[.](https://docs.rs/query/struct.SelectStatement.html#method.cond_having)

`SelectStatement::cond_having````
assert_eq!(
    Query::select()
        .column("id")
        .from("glyph")
        .cond_where(
            Cond::any()
                .add(
                    Cond::all()
                        .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_null())
                        .add(Expr::col("image").is_null())
                )
                .add(
                    Cond::all()
                        .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_in([3, 4]))
                        .add(Expr::col("image").like("A%"))
                )
        )
        .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"SELECT "id" FROM "glyph""#,
        r#"WHERE"#,
        r#"("aspect" IS NULL AND "image" IS NULL)"#,
        r#"OR"#,
        r#"("aspect" IN (3, 4) AND "image" LIKE 'A%')"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
```
There is also the [ any!](https://docs.rs/macro.any.html) and

[macro at your convenience:](https://docs.rs/macro.all.html)

`all!````
Query::select().cond_where(any![
    Expr::col(Glyph::Aspect).is_in([3, 4]),
    all![
        Expr::col(Glyph::Aspect).is_null(),
        Expr::col(Glyph::Image).like("A%")
    ]
]);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#statement-builders)Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [ QueryStatementBuilder](https://docs.rs/query/trait.QueryStatementBuilder.html) and

[respectively.](https://docs.rs/schema/trait.SchemaStatementBuilder.html)

`SchemaStatementBuilder`Schema statement has the following interface:

`fn build<T: SchemaBuilder>(&self, schema_builder: T) -> String;`Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
fn build<T: QueryBuilder>(&self, query_builder: T) -> (String, Values);
fn to_string<T: QueryBuilder>(&self, query_builder: T) -> String;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

[§](https://docs.rs#query-statement)Query Statement

[§](https://docs.rs#query-select)Query Select

```
let query = Query::select()
    .column("char_code")
    .column(("font", "name"))
    .from("character")
    .left_join("font", Expr::col(("character", "font_id")).equals(("font", "id")))
    .and_where(Expr::col("size_w").is_in([3, 4]))
    .and_where(Expr::col("char_code").like("A%"))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `char_code`, `font`.`name` FROM `character` LEFT JOIN `font` ON `character`.`font_id` = `font`.`id` WHERE `size_w` IN (3, 4) AND `char_code` LIKE 'A%'"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "char_code", "font"."name" FROM "character" LEFT JOIN "font" ON "character"."font_id" = "font"."id" WHERE "size_w" IN (3, 4) AND "char_code" LIKE 'A%'"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "char_code", "font"."name" FROM "character" LEFT JOIN "font" ON "character"."font_id" = "font"."id" WHERE "size_w" IN (3, 4) AND "char_code" LIKE 'A%'"#
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#query-insert)Query Insert

let query = Query::insert()
    .into_table(Glyph::Table)
    .columns([Glyph::Aspect, Glyph::Image])
    .values_panic([5.15.into(), "12A".into()])
    .values_panic([4.21.into(), "123".into()])
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(

    r#"INSERT INTO `glyph` (`aspect`, `image`) VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
);
```

let query = Query::update()
    .table(Glyph::Table)

[§](https://docs.rs#schema-statement)Schema Statement

[§](https://docs.rs#table-create)Table Create

```
let table = Table::create()
    .table("character")
    .if_not_exists()
    .col(ColumnDef::new("id").integer().not_null().auto_increment().primary_key())
    .col(ColumnDef::new("font_size").integer().not_null())
    .col(ColumnDef::new("character").string().not_null())
    .col(ColumnDef::new("size_w").integer().not_null())
    .col(ColumnDef::new("size_h").integer().not_null())
    .col(ColumnDef::new("font_id").integer().default(Expr::val(1)))
    .foreign_key(
        ForeignKey::create()
            .name("character_fk")
            .from("character", "font_id")
            .to("font", "id")
            .on_delete(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
            .on_update(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
    )
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `character` ("#,
            r#"`id` int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,"#,
            r#"`font_size` int NOT NULL,"#,
            r#"`character` varchar(255) NOT NULL,"#,
            r#"`size_w` int NOT NULL,"#,
            r#"`size_h` int NOT NULL,"#,
            r#"`font_id` int DEFAULT 1,"#,
            r#"CONSTRAINT `character_fk`"#,
                r#"FOREIGN KEY (`font_id`) REFERENCES `font` (`id`)"#,
                r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
        r#")"#,
    ].join(" ")
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "character" ("#,
            r#""id" integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,"#,
            r#""font_size" integer NOT NULL,"#,
            r#""character" varchar NOT NULL,"#,
            r#""size_w" integer NOT NULL,"#,
            r#""size_h" integer NOT NULL,"#,
            r#""font_id" integer DEFAULT 1,"#,
            r#"CONSTRAINT "character_fk""#,
                r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id")"#,
                r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
        r#")"#,
    ].join(" ")
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    [
       r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "character" ("#,
           r#""id" integer NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,"#,
           r#""font_size" integer NOT NULL,"#,
           r#""character" varchar NOT NULL,"#,
           r#""size_w" integer NOT NULL,"#,
           r#""size_h" integer NOT NULL,"#,
           r#""font_id" integer DEFAULT 1,"#,
           r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
       r#")"#,
    ].join(" ")
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#table-alter)Table Alter

```
let table = Table::alter()
    .table(Font::Table)
    .add_column(ColumnDef::new("new_col").integer().not_null().default(100))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE `font` ADD COLUMN `new_col` int NOT NULL DEFAULT 100"#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE "font" ADD COLUMN "new_col" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 100"#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE "font" ADD COLUMN "new_col" integer NOT NULL DEFAULT 100"#,
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#table-drop)Table Drop

```
let table = Table::drop()
    .table(Glyph::Table)
    .table(Char::Table)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"DROP TABLE `glyph`, `character`"#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"DROP TABLE "glyph", "character""#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"DROP TABLE "glyph", "character""#
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#table-rename)Table Rename

```
let table = Table::rename().table(Font::Table, "font_new").to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"RENAME TABLE `font` TO `font_new`"#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE "font" RENAME TO "font_new""#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE "font" RENAME TO "font_new""#
);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#table-truncate)Table Truncate

```
let table = Table::truncate().table(Font::Table).to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"TRUNCATE TABLE `font`"#
);
assert_eq!(
    table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"TRUNCATE TABLE "font""#
);
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
[§](https://docs.rs#foreign-key-create)Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = ForeignKey::create()
    .name("FK_character_font")
    .from(Char::Table, Char::FontId)
    .to(Font::Table, Font::Id)
    .on_delete(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
    .on_update(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"ALTER TABLE `character`"#,
        r#"ADD CONSTRAINT `FK_character_font`"#,
        r#"FOREIGN KEY (`font_id`) REFERENCES `font` (`id`)"#,
        r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    [
        r#"ALTER TABLE "character" ADD CONSTRAINT "FK_character_font""#,
        r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id")"#,
        r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
    ]
    .join(" ")
);
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
[§](https://docs.rs#foreign-key-drop)Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = ForeignKey::drop()
    .name("FK_character_font")
    .table(Char::Table)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE `character` DROP FOREIGN KEY `FK_character_font`"#
);
assert_eq!(
    foreign_key.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"ALTER TABLE "character" DROP CONSTRAINT "FK_character_font""#
);
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [audit](https://docs.rs/audit/index.html)- `audit`
- [backend](https://docs.rs/backend/index.html)
- Translating the SQL AST into engine-specific SQL statements.
- [error](https://docs.rs/error/index.html)
- Error types used in sea-query.
- [expr](https://docs.rs/expr/index.html)
- Building blocks of SQL statements.
- [extension](https://docs.rs/extension/index.html)
- Engine specific SQL features.
- [foreign_](https://docs.rs/foreign_key/index.html)- key
- Foreign key definition & alternations statements.
- [func](https://docs.rs/func/index.html)
- For calling built-in SQL functions.
- [index](https://docs.rs/index/index.html)
- Index definition & alternations statements.
- [prepare](https://docs.rs/prepare/index.html)
- Helper for preparing SQL statements.
- [query](https://docs.rs/query/index.html)
- Query statements (select, insert, update & delete).
- [raw_sql](https://docs.rs/raw_sql/index.html)
- [schema](https://docs.rs/schema/index.html)
- Schema definition & alternations statements
- [sqlx](https://docs.rs/sqlx/index.html)- `sqlx-utils`
- [table](https://docs.rs/table/index.html)
- Table definition & alternations statements.
- [token](https://docs.rs/token/index.html)
- [types](https://docs.rs/types/index.html)
- Base types used throughout sea-query.
- [value](https://docs.rs/value/index.html)
- Container for all SQL value types.

[27](https://docs.rs#27)//! ## SeaQuery
[28](https://docs.rs#28)//!
[29](https://docs.rs#29)//! SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust.
[30](https://docs.rs#30)//! You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API.
[31](https://docs.rs#31)//! We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.
[32](https://docs.rs#32)//! MS SQL Server Support is available under [SeaORM X](https://www.sea-ql.org/SeaORM-X/).
[33](https://docs.rs#33)//!
[34](https://docs.rs#34)//! SeaQuery is written in 100% safe Rust. All workspace crates has `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`.
[35](https://docs.rs#35)//!
[36](https://docs.rs#36)//! SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.
[37](https://docs.rs#37)//! We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[38](https://docs.rs#38)//! [postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
[39](https://docs.rs#39)//! See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.
[40](https://docs.rs#40)//!
[41](https://docs.rs#41)//! [![GitHub stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/SeaQL/sea-query.svg?style=social&label=Star&maxAge=1)](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)
[42](https://docs.rs#42)//! If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!
[43](https://docs.rs#43)//!
[44](https://docs.rs#44)//! [![Discord](https://img.shields.io/discord/873880840487206962?label=Discord)](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)
[45](https://docs.rs#45)//! Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!
[46](https://docs.rs#46)//!
[47](https://docs.rs#47)//! ## Install
[48](https://docs.rs#48)//!
[49](https://docs.rs#49)//! ```toml
[50](https://docs.rs#50)//! # Cargo.toml
[51](https://docs.rs#51)//! [dependencies]
[52](https://docs.rs#52)//! sea-query = "1.0"
[53](https://docs.rs#53)//! ```
[54](https://docs.rs#54)//!
[55](https://docs.rs#55)//! SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional.

[101](https://docs.rs#101)//! ## Motivation
[102](https://docs.rs#102)//!
[103](https://docs.rs#103)//! Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?
[104](https://docs.rs#104)//!
[105](https://docs.rs#105)//! ### 1. Parameter bindings
[106](https://docs.rs#106)//!
[107](https://docs.rs#107)//! One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can inject parameters
[108](https://docs.rs#108)//! right alongside the expression, and the $N sequencing will be handled for you. No more "off by one" errors!
[109](https://docs.rs#109)//!
[110](https://docs.rs#110)//! ```
[111](https://docs.rs#111)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[112](https://docs.rs#112)//! assert_eq!(
[113](https://docs.rs#113)//!     Query::select()
[114](https://docs.rs#114)//!         .expr(Expr::col("size_w").add(1).mul(2))
[115](https://docs.rs#115)//!         .from("glyph")
[116](https://docs.rs#116)//!         .and_where(Expr::col("image").like("A"))
[117](https://docs.rs#117)//!         .and_where(Expr::col("id").is_in([3, 4, 5]))
[118](https://docs.rs#118)//!         .build(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[119](https://docs.rs#119)//!     (
[120](https://docs.rs#120)//!         r#"SELECT ("size_w" + $1) * $2 FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE $3 AND "id" IN ($4, $5, $6)"#
[121](https://docs.rs#121)//!             .to_owned(),
[122](https://docs.rs#122)//!         Values(vec![
[123](https://docs.rs#123)//!             1.into(),
[124](https://docs.rs#124)//!             2.into(),
[125](https://docs.rs#125)//!             "A".to_owned().into(),
[126](https://docs.rs#126)//!             3.into(),
[127](https://docs.rs#127)//!             4.into(),
[128](https://docs.rs#128)//!             5.into(),
[129](https://docs.rs#129)//!         ])
[130](https://docs.rs#130)//!     )
[131](https://docs.rs#131)//! );
[132](https://docs.rs#132)//! ```
[133](https://docs.rs#133)//!
[134](https://docs.rs#134)//! If you need an "escape hatch" to construct complex queries, you can use custom expressions,
[135](https://docs.rs#135)//! and still have the benefit of sequentially-binded parameters.
[136](https://docs.rs#136)//!
[137](https://docs.rs#137)//! ```
[138](https://docs.rs#138)//! # use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
[139](https://docs.rs#139)//! assert_eq!(
[140](https://docs.rs#140)//!     Query::select()
[141](https://docs.rs#141)//!         .columns(["size_w", "size_h"])
[142](https://docs.rs#142)//!         .from("character")
[143](https://docs.rs#143)//!         .and_where(Expr::col("id").eq(1)) // this is $1
[144](https://docs.rs#144)//!         // custom expressions only need to define local parameter sequence.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)//!         // its global sequence will be re-written.
[146](https://docs.rs#146)//!         // here, we flip the order of $2 & $1 to make it look tricker!
[147](https://docs.rs#147)//!         .and_where(Expr::cust_with_values(r#""size_w" = $2 * $1"#, [3, 2]))
[148](https://docs.rs#148)//!         .and_where(Expr::col("size_h").gt(4)) // this is $N?
[149](https://docs.rs#149)//!         .build(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[150](https://docs.rs#150)//!     (
[151](https://docs.rs#151)//!         r#"SELECT "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "id" = $1 AND ("size_w" = $2 * $3) AND "size_h" > $4"#
[152](https://docs.rs#152)//!             .to_owned(),
[153](https://docs.rs#153)//!         Values(vec![1.into(), 2.into(), 3.into(), 4.into()])
[154](https://docs.rs#154)//!     )
[155](https://docs.rs#155)//! );
[156](https://docs.rs#156)//! ```
[157](https://docs.rs#157)//!
[158](https://docs.rs#158)//! ### 2. Dynamic query
[159](https://docs.rs#159)//!
[160](https://docs.rs#160)//! You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs with a fluent interface,
[161](https://docs.rs#161)//! so you don't have to append `WHERE` or `AND` conditionally.
[162](https://docs.rs#162)//!
[163](https://docs.rs#163)//! ```
[164](https://docs.rs#164)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[165](https://docs.rs#165)//! fn query(a: Option<i32>, b: Option<char>) -> SelectStatement {
[166](https://docs.rs#166)//!     Query::select()
[167](https://docs.rs#167)//!         .column("id")
[168](https://docs.rs#168)//!         .from("character")
[169](https://docs.rs#169)//!         .apply_if(a, |q, v| {
[170](https://docs.rs#170)//!             q.and_where(Expr::col("font_id").eq(v));
[171](https://docs.rs#171)//!         })
[172](https://docs.rs#172)//!         .apply_if(b, |q, v| {
[173](https://docs.rs#173)//!             q.and_where(Expr::col("ascii").like(v));
[174](https://docs.rs#174)//!         })
[175](https://docs.rs#175)//!         .take()
[176](https://docs.rs#176)//! }
[177](https://docs.rs#177)//!
[178](https://docs.rs#178)//! assert_eq!(
[179](https://docs.rs#179)//!     query(Some(5), Some('A')).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[180](https://docs.rs#180)//!     "SELECT `id` FROM `character` WHERE `font_id` = 5 AND `ascii` LIKE 'A'"
[181](https://docs.rs#181)//! );
[182](https://docs.rs#182)//! assert_eq!(
[183](https://docs.rs#183)//!     query(Some(5), None).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[184](https://docs.rs#184)//!     "SELECT `id` FROM `character` WHERE `font_id` = 5"
[185](https://docs.rs#185)//! );
[186](https://docs.rs#186)//! assert_eq!(
[187](https://docs.rs#187)//!     query(None, None).to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[188](https://docs.rs#188)//!     "SELECT `id` FROM `character`"
[189](https://docs.rs#189)//! );
[190](https://docs.rs#190)//! ```
[191](https://docs.rs#191)//!
[192](https://docs.rs#192)//! Conditions can be arbitrarily complex, thanks to SeaQuery's internal AST:
[193](https://docs.rs#193)//!
[194](https://docs.rs#194)//! ```
[195](https://docs.rs#195)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[196](https://docs.rs#196)//! assert_eq!(
[197](https://docs.rs#197)//!     Query::select()
[198](https://docs.rs#198)//!         .column("id")
[199](https://docs.rs#199)//!         .from("glyph")
[200](https://docs.rs#200)//!         .cond_where(
[201](https://docs.rs#201)//!             Cond::any()
[202](https://docs.rs#202)//!                 .add(
[203](https://docs.rs#203)//!                     Cond::all()
[204](https://docs.rs#204)//!                         .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_null())
[205](https://docs.rs#205)//!                         .add(Expr::col("image").is_null())
[206](https://docs.rs#206)//!                 )
[207](https://docs.rs#207)//!                 .add(
[208](https://docs.rs#208)//!                     Cond::all()
[209](https://docs.rs#209)//!                         .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_in([3, 4]))
[210](https://docs.rs#210)//!                         .add(Expr::col("image").like("A%"))
[211](https://docs.rs#211)//!                 )
[212](https://docs.rs#212)//!         )
[213](https://docs.rs#213)//!         .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[214](https://docs.rs#214)//!     [
[215](https://docs.rs#215)//!         r#"SELECT "id" FROM "glyph""#,
[216](https://docs.rs#216)//!         r#"WHERE"#,
[217](https://docs.rs#217)//!         r#"("aspect" IS NULL AND "image" IS NULL)"#,
[218](https://docs.rs#218)//!         r#"OR"#,
[219](https://docs.rs#219)//!         r#"("aspect" IN (3, 4) AND "image" LIKE 'A%')"#,
[220](https://docs.rs#220)//!     ]
[221](https://docs.rs#221)//!     .join(" ")
[222](https://docs.rs#222)//! );
[223](https://docs.rs#223)//! ```
[224](https://docs.rs#224)//!
[225](https://docs.rs#225)//! There is no superfluous parentheses `((((` cluttering the query, because SeaQuery respects
[226](https://docs.rs#226)//! operator precedence when injecting them.
[227](https://docs.rs#227)//!
[228](https://docs.rs#228)//! ### 3. Cross database support
[229](https://docs.rs#229)//!
[230](https://docs.rs#230)//! With SeaQuery, you can target multiple database backends while maintaining a single source of query logic.
[231](https://docs.rs#231)//!
[232](https://docs.rs#232)//! ```
[233](https://docs.rs#233)//! # use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
[234](https://docs.rs#234)//! let query = Query::insert()
[235](https://docs.rs#235)//!     .into_table("glyph")
[236](https://docs.rs#236)//!     .columns(["aspect", "image"])
[237](https://docs.rs#237)//!     .values_panic([
[238](https://docs.rs#238)//!         2.into(),
[239](https://docs.rs#239)//!         3.into(),
[240](https://docs.rs#240)//!     ])
[241](https://docs.rs#241)//!     .on_conflict(
[242](https://docs.rs#242)//!         OnConflict::column("id")
[243](https://docs.rs#243)//!             .update_columns(["aspect", "image"])
[244](https://docs.rs#244)//!             .to_owned(),
[245](https://docs.rs#245)//!     )
[246](https://docs.rs#246)//!     .to_owned();
[247](https://docs.rs#247)//!
[248](https://docs.rs#248)//! assert_eq!(
[249](https://docs.rs#249)//!     query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[250](https://docs.rs#250)//!     r#"INSERT INTO `glyph` (`aspect`, `image`) VALUES (2, 3) ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE `aspect` = VALUES(`aspect`), `image` = VALUES(`image`)"#
[251](https://docs.rs#251)//! );
[252](https://docs.rs#252)//! assert_eq!(
[253](https://docs.rs#253)//!     query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[254](https://docs.rs#254)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (2, 3) ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE SET "aspect" = "excluded"."aspect", "image" = "excluded"."image""#
[255](https://docs.rs#255)//! );
[256](https://docs.rs#256)//! assert_eq!(
[257](https://docs.rs#257)//!     query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[258](https://docs.rs#258)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (2, 3) ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE SET "aspect" = "excluded"."aspect", "image" = "excluded"."image""#
[259](https://docs.rs#259)//! );
[260](https://docs.rs#260)//! ```
[261](https://docs.rs#261)//!
[262](https://docs.rs#262)//! ### 4. Improved raw SQL ergonomics
[263](https://docs.rs#263)//!
[264](https://docs.rs#264)//! SeaQuery 1.0 added a new `raw_query!` macro with named parameters, nested field access, array expansion and tuple expansion.
[265](https://docs.rs#265)//! It surely will make crafting complex query easier.
[266](https://docs.rs#266)//!
[267](https://docs.rs#267)//! ```
[268](https://docs.rs#268)//! # use sea_query::Values;
[269](https://docs.rs#269)//! let (a, b, c) = (1, 2, "A");
[270](https://docs.rs#270)//! let d = vec![3, 4, 5];
[271](https://docs.rs#271)//! let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
[272](https://docs.rs#272)//!     PostgresQueryBuilder,
[273](https://docs.rs#273)//!     r#"SELECT ("size_w" + {a}) * {b} FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE {c} AND "id" IN ({..d})"#
[274](https://docs.rs#274)//! );
[275](https://docs.rs#275)//!
[276](https://docs.rs#276)//! assert_eq!(
[277](https://docs.rs#277)//!     query.sql,
[278](https://docs.rs#278)//!     r#"SELECT ("size_w" + $1) * $2 FROM "glyph" WHERE "image" LIKE $3 AND "id" IN ($4, $5, $6)"#
[279](https://docs.rs#279)//! );
[280](https://docs.rs#280)//! assert_eq!(
[281](https://docs.rs#281)//!     query.values,
[282](https://docs.rs#282)//!     Values(vec![
[283](https://docs.rs#283)//!         1.into(),
[284](https://docs.rs#284)//!         2.into(),
[285](https://docs.rs#285)//!         "A".into(),
[286](https://docs.rs#286)//!         3.into(),
[287](https://docs.rs#287)//!         4.into(),
[288](https://docs.rs#288)//!         5.into()
[289](https://docs.rs#289)//!     ])
[290](https://docs.rs#290)//! );
[291](https://docs.rs#291)//! ```
[292](https://docs.rs#292)//!
[293](https://docs.rs#293)//! Insert with vector-of-tuple expansion.
[294](https://docs.rs#294)//!
[295](https://docs.rs#295)//! ```
[296](https://docs.rs#296)//! # use sea_query::Values;
[297](https://docs.rs#297)//! let values = vec![(2.1345, "24B"), (5.15, "12A")];
[298](https://docs.rs#298)//! let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
[299](https://docs.rs#299)//!     PostgresQueryBuilder,
[300](https://docs.rs#300)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES {..(values.0:1),}"#
[301](https://docs.rs#301)//! );
[302](https://docs.rs#302)//!
[303](https://docs.rs#303)//! assert_eq!(
[304](https://docs.rs#304)//!     query.sql,
[305](https://docs.rs#305)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES ($1, $2), ($3, $4)"#
[306](https://docs.rs#306)//! );
[307](https://docs.rs#307)//! assert_eq!(
[308](https://docs.rs#308)//!     query.values,
[309](https://docs.rs#309)//!     Values(vec![2.1345.into(), "24B".into(), 5.15.into(), "12A".into()])
[310](https://docs.rs#310)//! );
[311](https://docs.rs#311)//! ```
[312](https://docs.rs#312)//!
[313](https://docs.rs#313)//! Update with nested field access.
[314](https://docs.rs#314)//!
[315](https://docs.rs#315)//! ```
[316](https://docs.rs#316)//! # use sea_query::Values;
[317](https://docs.rs#317)//! struct Character {
[318](https://docs.rs#318)//!     id: i32,
[319](https://docs.rs#319)//!     font_size: u16,
[320](https://docs.rs#320)//! }
[321](https://docs.rs#321)//! let c = Character {
[322](https://docs.rs#322)//!     id: 11,
[323](https://docs.rs#323)//!     font_size: 22,
[324](https://docs.rs#324)//! };
[325](https://docs.rs#325)//! let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
[326](https://docs.rs#326)//!     MysqlQueryBuilder,
[327](https://docs.rs#327)//!     "UPDATE `character` SET `font_size` = {c.font_size} WHERE `id` = {c.id}"
[328](https://docs.rs#328)//! );
[329](https://docs.rs#329)//!
[330](https://docs.rs#330)//! assert_eq!(
[331](https://docs.rs#331)//!     query.sql,
[332](https://docs.rs#332)//!     "UPDATE `character` SET `font_size` = ? WHERE `id` = ?"
[333](https://docs.rs#333)//! );
[334](https://docs.rs#334)//! assert_eq!(query.values, Values(vec![22u16.into(), 11i32.into()]));
[335](https://docs.rs#335)//! ```
[336](https://docs.rs#336)//!
[337](https://docs.rs#337)//! ## Basics
[338](https://docs.rs#338)//!
[339](https://docs.rs#339)//! ### Iden
[340](https://docs.rs#340)//!
[341](https://docs.rs#341)//! `Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.
[342](https://docs.rs#342)//!
[343](https://docs.rs#343)//! Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database,
[344](https://docs.rs#344)//! and its variants include table name and column name.
[345](https://docs.rs#345)//!
[346](https://docs.rs#346)//! You can use the `Iden` derive macro to implement it.
[347](https://docs.rs#347)//!
[348](https://docs.rs#348)//! ```rust
[349](https://docs.rs#349)//! # use sea_query::Iden;
[350](https://docs.rs#350)//! #[derive(Iden)]
[351](https://docs.rs#351)//! enum Character {
[352](https://docs.rs#352)//!     Table,
[353](https://docs.rs#353)//!     Id,
[354](https://docs.rs#354)//!     FontId,
[355](https://docs.rs#355)//!     FontSize,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)//! }
[357](https://docs.rs#357)//!
[358](https://docs.rs#358)//! assert_eq!(Character::Table.to_string(), "character");
[359](https://docs.rs#359)//! assert_eq!(Character::Id.to_string(), "id");
[360](https://docs.rs#360)//! assert_eq!(Character::FontId.to_string(), "font_id");
[361](https://docs.rs#361)//! assert_eq!(Character::FontSize.to_string(), "font_size");
[362](https://docs.rs#362)//!
[363](https://docs.rs#363)//! #[derive(Iden)]
[364](https://docs.rs#364)//! struct Glyph;
[365](https://docs.rs#365)//! assert_eq!(Glyph.to_string(), "glyph");
[366](https://docs.rs#366)//! ```
[367](https://docs.rs#367)//!
[368](https://docs.rs#368)//! ```rust
[369](https://docs.rs#369)//! use sea_query::{Iden, enum_def};
[370](https://docs.rs#370)//!
[371](https://docs.rs#371)//! #[enum_def]
[372](https://docs.rs#372)//! struct Character {
[373](https://docs.rs#373)//!     pub foo: u64,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)//! }
[375](https://docs.rs#375)//!
[376](https://docs.rs#376)//! // It generates the following along with Iden impl
[377](https://docs.rs#377)//! # let not_real = || {
[378](https://docs.rs#378)//! enum CharacterIden {
[379](https://docs.rs#379)//!     Table,
[380](https://docs.rs#380)//!     Foo,
[381](https://docs.rs#381)//! }
[382](https://docs.rs#382)//! # };
[383](https://docs.rs#383)//!
[384](https://docs.rs#384)//! assert_eq!(CharacterIden::Table.to_string(), "character");
[385](https://docs.rs#385)//! assert_eq!(CharacterIden::Foo.to_string(), "foo");
[386](https://docs.rs#386)//! ```
[387](https://docs.rs#387)//!
[388](https://docs.rs#388)//! ### Expression
[389](https://docs.rs#389)//!
[390](https://docs.rs#390)//! Use [`Expr`] constructors and [`ExprTrait`] methods
[391](https://docs.rs#391)//! to construct `SELECT`, `JOIN`, `WHERE` and `HAVING` expression in query.
[392](https://docs.rs#392)//!
[393](https://docs.rs#393)//! ```rust
[394](https://docs.rs#394)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[395](https://docs.rs#395)//! assert_eq!(
[396](https://docs.rs#396)//!     Query::select()
[397](https://docs.rs#397)//!         .column("char_code")
[398](https://docs.rs#398)//!         .from("character")
[399](https://docs.rs#399)//!         .and_where(
[400](https://docs.rs#400)//!             Expr::col("size_w")
[401](https://docs.rs#401)//!                 .add(1)
[402](https://docs.rs#402)//!                 .mul(2)
[403](https://docs.rs#403)//!                 .eq(Expr::col("size_h").div(2).sub(1))
[404](https://docs.rs#404)//!         )
[405](https://docs.rs#405)//!         .and_where(
[406](https://docs.rs#406)//!             Expr::col("size_w").in_subquery(
[407](https://docs.rs#407)//!                 Query::select()
[408](https://docs.rs#408)//!                     .expr(Expr::cust_with_values("ln($1 ^ $2)", [2.4, 1.2]))
[409](https://docs.rs#409)//!                     .take()
[410](https://docs.rs#410)//!             )
[411](https://docs.rs#411)//!         )
[412](https://docs.rs#412)//!         .and_where(
[413](https://docs.rs#413)//!             Expr::col("char_code")
[414](https://docs.rs#414)//!                 .like("D")
[415](https://docs.rs#415)//!                 .and(Expr::col("char_code").like("E"))
[416](https://docs.rs#416)//!         )
[417](https://docs.rs#417)//!         .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[418](https://docs.rs#418)//!     [
[419](https://docs.rs#419)//!         r#"SELECT "char_code" FROM "character""#,
[420](https://docs.rs#420)//!         r#"WHERE ("size_w" + 1) * 2 = ("size_h" / 2) - 1"#,
[421](https://docs.rs#421)//!         r#"AND "size_w" IN (SELECT ln(2.4 ^ 1.2))"#,
[422](https://docs.rs#422)//!         r#"AND ("char_code" LIKE 'D' AND "char_code" LIKE 'E')"#,
[423](https://docs.rs#423)//!     ]
[424](https://docs.rs#424)//!     .join(" ")
[425](https://docs.rs#425)//! );
[426](https://docs.rs#426)//! ```
[427](https://docs.rs#427)//!
[428](https://docs.rs#428)//! ### Condition
[429](https://docs.rs#429)//!
[430](https://docs.rs#430)//! If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
[431](https://docs.rs#431)//! usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].
[432](https://docs.rs#432)//!
[433](https://docs.rs#433)//! ```
[434](https://docs.rs#434)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[435](https://docs.rs#435)//! assert_eq!(
[436](https://docs.rs#436)//!     Query::select()
[437](https://docs.rs#437)//!         .column("id")
[438](https://docs.rs#438)//!         .from("glyph")
[439](https://docs.rs#439)//!         .cond_where(
[440](https://docs.rs#440)//!             Cond::any()
[441](https://docs.rs#441)//!                 .add(
[442](https://docs.rs#442)//!                     Cond::all()
[443](https://docs.rs#443)//!                         .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_null())
[444](https://docs.rs#444)//!                         .add(Expr::col("image").is_null())
[445](https://docs.rs#445)//!                 )
[446](https://docs.rs#446)//!                 .add(
[447](https://docs.rs#447)//!                     Cond::all()
[448](https://docs.rs#448)//!                         .add(Expr::col("aspect").is_in([3, 4]))
[449](https://docs.rs#449)//!                         .add(Expr::col("image").like("A%"))
[450](https://docs.rs#450)//!                 )
[451](https://docs.rs#451)//!         )
[452](https://docs.rs#452)//!         .to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[453](https://docs.rs#453)//!     [
[454](https://docs.rs#454)//!         r#"SELECT "id" FROM "glyph""#,
[455](https://docs.rs#455)//!         r#"WHERE"#,
[456](https://docs.rs#456)//!         r#"("aspect" IS NULL AND "image" IS NULL)"#,
[457](https://docs.rs#457)//!         r#"OR"#,
[458](https://docs.rs#458)//!         r#"("aspect" IN (3, 4) AND "image" LIKE 'A%')"#,
[459](https://docs.rs#459)//!     ]
[460](https://docs.rs#460)//!     .join(" ")
[461](https://docs.rs#461)//! );
[462](https://docs.rs#462)//! ```
[463](https://docs.rs#463)//!
[464](https://docs.rs#464)//! There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:
[465](https://docs.rs#465)//!
[466](https://docs.rs#466)//! ```
[467](https://docs.rs#467)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[468](https://docs.rs#468)//! Query::select().cond_where(any![
[469](https://docs.rs#469)//!     Expr::col(Glyph::Aspect).is_in([3, 4]),
[470](https://docs.rs#470)//!     all![
[471](https://docs.rs#471)//!         Expr::col(Glyph::Aspect).is_null(),
[472](https://docs.rs#472)//!         Expr::col(Glyph::Image).like("A%")
[473](https://docs.rs#473)//!     ]
[474](https://docs.rs#474)//! ]);
[475](https://docs.rs#475)//! ```
[476](https://docs.rs#476)//!
[477](https://docs.rs#477)//! ### Statement Builders
[478](https://docs.rs#478)//!
[479](https://docs.rs#479)//! Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
[480](https://docs.rs#480)//! with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.
[481](https://docs.rs#481)//!
[482](https://docs.rs#482)//! Schema statement has the following interface:
[483](https://docs.rs#483)//!
[484](https://docs.rs#484)//! ```rust
[485](https://docs.rs#485)//! # use sea_query::{*};
[486](https://docs.rs#486)//! # trait ExampleSchemaBuilder {
[487](https://docs.rs#487)//! fn build<T: SchemaBuilder>(&self, schema_builder: T) -> String;
[488](https://docs.rs#488)//! # }
[489](https://docs.rs#489)//! ```
[490](https://docs.rs#490)//!
[491](https://docs.rs#491)//! Query statement has the following interfaces:
[492](https://docs.rs#492)//!
[493](https://docs.rs#493)//! ```rust
[494](https://docs.rs#494)//! # use sea_query::{*};
[495](https://docs.rs#495)//! # trait ExampleQueryBuilder {
[496](https://docs.rs#496)//! fn build<T: QueryBuilder>(&self, query_builder: T) -> (String, Values);
[497](https://docs.rs#497)//!
[498](https://docs.rs#498)//! fn to_string<T: QueryBuilder>(&self, query_builder: T) -> String;
[499](https://docs.rs#499)//! # }
[500](https://docs.rs#500)//! ```
[501](https://docs.rs#501)//!
[502](https://docs.rs#502)//! `build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
[503](https://docs.rs#503)//! through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.
[504](https://docs.rs#504)//!
[505](https://docs.rs#505)//! `to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
[506](https://docs.rs#506)//! and debugging.
[507](https://docs.rs#507)//!
[508](https://docs.rs#508)//! ## Query Statement
[509](https://docs.rs#509)//!
[510](https://docs.rs#510)//! ### Query Select
[511](https://docs.rs#511)//!
[512](https://docs.rs#512)//! ```rust
[513](https://docs.rs#513)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[514](https://docs.rs#514)//! let query = Query::select()
[515](https://docs.rs#515)//!     .column("char_code")
[516](https://docs.rs#516)//!     .column(("font", "name"))
[517](https://docs.rs#517)//!     .from("character")
[518](https://docs.rs#518)//!     .left_join("font", Expr::col(("character", "font_id")).equals(("font", "id")))
[519](https://docs.rs#519)//!     .and_where(Expr::col("size_w").is_in([3, 4]))
[520](https://docs.rs#520)//!     .and_where(Expr::col("char_code").like("A%"))
[521](https://docs.rs#521)//!     .to_owned();
[522](https://docs.rs#522)//!
[523](https://docs.rs#523)//! assert_eq!(
[524](https://docs.rs#524)//!     query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[525](https://docs.rs#525)//!     r#"SELECT `char_code`, `font`.`name` FROM `character` LEFT JOIN `font` ON `character`.`font_id` = `font`.`id` WHERE `size_w` IN (3, 4) AND `char_code` LIKE 'A%'"#
[526](https://docs.rs#526)//! );
[527](https://docs.rs#527)//! assert_eq!(
[528](https://docs.rs#528)//!     query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[529](https://docs.rs#529)//!     r#"SELECT "char_code", "font"."name" FROM "character" LEFT JOIN "font" ON "character"."font_id" = "font"."id" WHERE "size_w" IN (3, 4) AND "char_code" LIKE 'A%'"#
[530](https://docs.rs#530)//! );
[531](https://docs.rs#531)//! assert_eq!(
[532](https://docs.rs#532)//!     query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[533](https://docs.rs#533)//!     r#"SELECT "char_code", "font"."name" FROM "character" LEFT JOIN "font" ON "character"."font_id" = "font"."id" WHERE "size_w" IN (3, 4) AND "char_code" LIKE 'A%'"#
[534](https://docs.rs#534)//! );
[535](https://docs.rs#535)//! ```
[536](https://docs.rs#536)//!
[537](https://docs.rs#537)//! ### Query Insert
[538](https://docs.rs#538)//!
[539](https://docs.rs#539)//! ```rust
[540](https://docs.rs#540)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[541](https://docs.rs#541)//! let query = Query::insert()
[542](https://docs.rs#542)//!     .into_table(Glyph::Table)
[543](https://docs.rs#543)//!     .columns([Glyph::Aspect, Glyph::Image])
[544](https://docs.rs#544)//!     .values_panic([5.15.into(), "12A".into()])
[545](https://docs.rs#545)//!     .values_panic([4.21.into(), "123".into()])
[546](https://docs.rs#546)//!     .to_owned();
[547](https://docs.rs#547)//!
[548](https://docs.rs#548)//! assert_eq!(
[549](https://docs.rs#549)//!     query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[550](https://docs.rs#550)//!     r#"INSERT INTO `glyph` (`aspect`, `image`) VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
[551](https://docs.rs#551)//! );
[552](https://docs.rs#552)//! assert_eq!(
[553](https://docs.rs#553)//!     query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[554](https://docs.rs#554)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
[555](https://docs.rs#555)//! );
[556](https://docs.rs#556)//! assert_eq!(
[557](https://docs.rs#557)//!     query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[558](https://docs.rs#558)//!     r#"INSERT INTO "glyph" ("aspect", "image") VALUES (5.15, '12A'), (4.21, '123')"#
[559](https://docs.rs#559)//! );
[560](https://docs.rs#560)//! ```
[561](https://docs.rs#561)//!
[562](https://docs.rs#562)//! ### Query Update
[563](https://docs.rs#563)//!
[564](https://docs.rs#564)//! ```rust
[565](https://docs.rs#565)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[566](https://docs.rs#566)//! let query = Query::update()
[567](https://docs.rs#567)//!     .table(Glyph::Table)
[568](https://docs.rs#568)//!     .values([(Glyph::Aspect, 1.23.into()), (Glyph::Image, "123".into())])
[569](https://docs.rs#569)//!     .and_where(Expr::col(Glyph::Id).eq(1))
[570](https://docs.rs#570)//!     .to_owned();
[571](https://docs.rs#571)//!
[572](https://docs.rs#572)//! assert_eq!(
[573](https://docs.rs#573)//!     query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[574](https://docs.rs#574)//!     r#"UPDATE `glyph` SET `aspect` = 1.23, `image` = '123' WHERE `id` = 1"#
[575](https://docs.rs#575)//! );
[576](https://docs.rs#576)//! assert_eq!(
[577](https://docs.rs#577)//!     query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[578](https://docs.rs#578)//!     r#"UPDATE "glyph" SET "aspect" = 1.23, "image" = '123' WHERE "id" = 1"#
[579](https://docs.rs#579)//! );
[580](https://docs.rs#580)//! assert_eq!(
[581](https://docs.rs#581)//!     query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[582](https://docs.rs#582)//!     r#"UPDATE "glyph" SET "aspect" = 1.23, "image" = '123' WHERE "id" = 1"#
[583](https://docs.rs#583)//! );
[584](https://docs.rs#584)//! ```

[586](https://docs.rs#586)//! ### Query Delete
[587](https://docs.rs#587)//!
[588](https://docs.rs#588)//! ```rust
[589](https://docs.rs#589)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[590](https://docs.rs#590)//! let query = Query::delete()
[591](https://docs.rs#591)//!     .from_table(Glyph::Table)
[592](https://docs.rs#592)//!     .cond_where(
[593](https://docs.rs#593)//!         Cond::any()
[594](https://docs.rs#594)//!             .add(Expr::col(Glyph::Id).lt(1))
[595](https://docs.rs#595)//!             .add(Expr::col(Glyph::Id).gt(10)),
[596](https://docs.rs#596)//!     )
[597](https://docs.rs#597)//!     .to_owned();
[598](https://docs.rs#598)//!
[599](https://docs.rs#599)//! assert_eq!(
[600](https://docs.rs#600)//!     query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[601](https://docs.rs#601)//!     r#"DELETE FROM `glyph` WHERE `id` < 1 OR `id` > 10"#
[602](https://docs.rs#602)//! );
[603](https://docs.rs#603)//! assert_eq!(
[604](https://docs.rs#604)//!     query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[605](https://docs.rs#605)//!     r#"DELETE FROM "glyph" WHERE "id" < 1 OR "id" > 10"#
[606](https://docs.rs#606)//! );
[607](https://docs.rs#607)//! assert_eq!(
[608](https://docs.rs#608)//!     query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[609](https://docs.rs#609)//!     r#"DELETE FROM "glyph" WHERE "id" < 1 OR "id" > 10"#
[610](https://docs.rs#610)//! );
[611](https://docs.rs#611)//! ```

[691](https://docs.rs#691)//! ## Schema Statement
[692](https://docs.rs#692)//!
[693](https://docs.rs#693)//! ### Table Create
[694](https://docs.rs#694)//!
[695](https://docs.rs#695)//! ```rust
[696](https://docs.rs#696)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[697](https://docs.rs#697)//! let table = Table::create()
[698](https://docs.rs#698)//!     .table("character")
[699](https://docs.rs#699)//!     .if_not_exists()
[700](https://docs.rs#700)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("id").integer().not_null().auto_increment().primary_key())
[701](https://docs.rs#701)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("font_size").integer().not_null())
[702](https://docs.rs#702)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("character").string().not_null())
[703](https://docs.rs#703)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("size_w").integer().not_null())
[704](https://docs.rs#704)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("size_h").integer().not_null())
[705](https://docs.rs#705)//!     .col(ColumnDef::new("font_id").integer().default(Expr::val(1)))
[706](https://docs.rs#706)//!     .foreign_key(
[707](https://docs.rs#707)//!         ForeignKey::create()
[708](https://docs.rs#708)//!             .name("character_fk")
[709](https://docs.rs#709)//!             .from("character", "font_id")
[710](https://docs.rs#710)//!             .to("font", "id")
[711](https://docs.rs#711)//!             .on_delete(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
[712](https://docs.rs#712)//!             .on_update(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
[713](https://docs.rs#713)//!     )
[714](https://docs.rs#714)//!     .to_owned();
[715](https://docs.rs#715)//!
[716](https://docs.rs#716)//! assert_eq!(
[717](https://docs.rs#717)//!     table.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[718](https://docs.rs#718)//!     [
[719](https://docs.rs#719)//!         r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS `character` ("#,
[720](https://docs.rs#720)//!             r#"`id` int NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTO_INCREMENT,"#,
[721](https://docs.rs#721)//!             r#"`font_size` int NOT NULL,"#,
[722](https://docs.rs#722)//!             r#"`character` varchar(255) NOT NULL,"#,
[723](https://docs.rs#723)//!             r#"`size_w` int NOT NULL,"#,
[724](https://docs.rs#724)//!             r#"`size_h` int NOT NULL,"#,
[725](https://docs.rs#725)//!             r#"`font_id` int DEFAULT 1,"#,
[726](https://docs.rs#726)//!             r#"CONSTRAINT `character_fk`"#,
[727](https://docs.rs#727)//!                 r#"FOREIGN KEY (`font_id`) REFERENCES `font` (`id`)"#,
[728](https://docs.rs#728)//!                 r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
[729](https://docs.rs#729)//!         r#")"#,
[730](https://docs.rs#730)//!     ].join(" ")
[731](https://docs.rs#731)//! );
[732](https://docs.rs#732)//! assert_eq!(
[733](https://docs.rs#733)//!     table.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[734](https://docs.rs#734)//!     [
[735](https://docs.rs#735)//!         r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "character" ("#,
[736](https://docs.rs#736)//!             r#""id" integer GENERATED BY DEFAULT AS IDENTITY NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,"#,
[737](https://docs.rs#737)//!             r#""font_size" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[738](https://docs.rs#738)//!             r#""character" varchar NOT NULL,"#,
[739](https://docs.rs#739)//!             r#""size_w" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[740](https://docs.rs#740)//!             r#""size_h" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[741](https://docs.rs#741)//!             r#""font_id" integer DEFAULT 1,"#,
[742](https://docs.rs#742)//!             r#"CONSTRAINT "character_fk""#,
[743](https://docs.rs#743)//!                 r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id")"#,
[744](https://docs.rs#744)//!                 r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
[745](https://docs.rs#745)//!         r#")"#,
[746](https://docs.rs#746)//!     ].join(" ")
[747](https://docs.rs#747)//! );
[748](https://docs.rs#748)//! assert_eq!(
[749](https://docs.rs#749)//!     table.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
[750](https://docs.rs#750)//!     [
[751](https://docs.rs#751)//!        r#"CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS "character" ("#,
[752](https://docs.rs#752)//!            r#""id" integer NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,"#,
[753](https://docs.rs#753)//!            r#""font_size" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[754](https://docs.rs#754)//!            r#""character" varchar NOT NULL,"#,
[755](https://docs.rs#755)//!            r#""size_w" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[756](https://docs.rs#756)//!            r#""size_h" integer NOT NULL,"#,
[757](https://docs.rs#757)//!            r#""font_id" integer DEFAULT 1,"#,
[758](https://docs.rs#758)//!            r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id") ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
[759](https://docs.rs#759)//!        r#")"#,
[760](https://docs.rs#760)//!     ].join(" ")
[761](https://docs.rs#761)//! );
[762](https://docs.rs#762)//! ```
[763](https://docs.rs#763)//!

[847](https://docs.rs#847)//! ### Foreign Key Create
[848](https://docs.rs#848)//!
[849](https://docs.rs#849)//! ```rust
[850](https://docs.rs#850)//! # use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
[851](https://docs.rs#851)//! let foreign_key = ForeignKey::create()
[852](https://docs.rs#852)//!     .name("FK_character_font")
[853](https://docs.rs#853)//!     .from(Char::Table, Char::FontId)
[854](https://docs.rs#854)//!     .to(Font::Table, Font::Id)
[855](https://docs.rs#855)//!     .on_delete(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
[856](https://docs.rs#856)//!     .on_update(ForeignKeyAction::Cascade)
[857](https://docs.rs#857)//!     .to_owned();
[858](https://docs.rs#858)//!
[859](https://docs.rs#859)//! assert_eq!(
[860](https://docs.rs#860)//!     foreign_key.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
[861](https://docs.rs#861)//!     [
[862](https://docs.rs#862)//!         r#"ALTER TABLE `character`"#,
[863](https://docs.rs#863)//!         r#"ADD CONSTRAINT `FK_character_font`"#,
[864](https://docs.rs#864)//!         r#"FOREIGN KEY (`font_id`) REFERENCES `font` (`id`)"#,
[865](https://docs.rs#865)//!         r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
[866](https://docs.rs#866)//!     ]
[867](https://docs.rs#867)//!     .join(" ")
[868](https://docs.rs#868)//! );
[869](https://docs.rs#869)//! assert_eq!(
[870](https://docs.rs#870)//!     foreign_key.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
[871](https://docs.rs#871)//!     [
[872](https://docs.rs#872)//!         r#"ALTER TABLE "character" ADD CONSTRAINT "FK_character_font""#,
[873](https://docs.rs#873)//!         r#"FOREIGN KEY ("font_id") REFERENCES "font" ("id")"#,
[874](https://docs.rs#874)//!         r#"ON DELETE CASCADE ON UPDATE CASCADE"#,
[875](https://docs.rs#875)//!     ]
[876](https://docs.rs#876)//!     .join(" ")
[877](https://docs.rs#877)//! );
[878](https://docs.rs#878)//! // Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
[879](https://docs.rs#879)//! ```

[931](https://docs.rs#931)//!     .table(Glyph::Table)
[932](https://docs.rs#932)//!     .to_owned();
[933](https://docs.rs#933)//!
[934](https://docs.rs#934)//! assert_eq!(
[935](https://docs.rs#935)//!     index.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),

[937](https://docs.rs#937)//! );
[938](https://docs.rs#938)//! assert_eq!(
[939](https://docs.rs#939)//!     index.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),

}## Expand description

An arbitrary, dynamically-typed SQL expression.

It can be used in select fields, where clauses and many other places.

More concreterly, under the hood [ Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)s can be:

- Rust values
- SQL identifiers
- SQL function calls
- various operators and sub-queries

If something is not supported here, look into [ BinOper::Custom](https://docs.rs/types/enum.BinOper.html#variant.Custom),

[, or](https://docs.rs/func/enum.Func.html#method.cust)

`Func::cust`[as a workaround, and consider reporting your issue.](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html#method.cust_with_values)

#### pub fn [asterisk](https://docs.rs#method.asterisk)() -> Self

Express the target column without table prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(Expr::col(Char::SizeW).eq(1))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE `size_w` = 1"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" = 1"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" = 1"#
);
```
```

Wraps tuple of `Expr`, can be used for tuple comparison

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(
        Expr::tuple([Expr::col(Char::SizeW).into(), Expr::value(100)])
            .lt(Expr::tuple([Expr::value(500), Expr::value(100)])))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE (`size_w`, 100) < (500, 100)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE ("size_w", 100) < (500, 100)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE ("size_w", 100) < (500, 100)"#
);

Wrap an expression to perform some operation on it later.

Since `sea_query` 0.32.0 (`sea_orm` 1.1.1), **this is not necessary** in most cases!

Some SQL operations used to be defined only as inherent methods on [ Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html).
Thus, to use them, you needed to manually convert from other types to

[. But now these operations are also defined as](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)

`Expr`[methods that can be called directly on any expression type,](https://docs.rs/trait.ExprTrait.html)

`ExprTrait`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-4)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    // This is the old style, when `Expr::expr` was necessary:
    .and_where(Expr::expr(Expr::col(Char::SizeW).if_null(0)).gt(2))
    .to_owned();
// But since 0.32.0, this compiles too:
let _ = Expr::col(Char::SizeW).if_null(0).gt(2);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE IFNULL(`size_w`, 0) > 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE COALESCE("size_w", 0) > 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE IFNULL("size_w", 0) > 2"#
);
```
```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .column(Char::Character)
    .from(Char::Table)
    // This is the old style, when `Expr::expr` was necessary:
    .and_where(Expr::expr(Func::lower(Expr::col(Char::Character))).is_in(["a", "b"]))
    .to_owned();
// But since 0.32.0, this compiles too:
let _ = Func::lower(Expr::col(Char::Character)).is_in(["a", "b"]);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character` FROM `character` WHERE LOWER(`character`) IN ('a', 'b')"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character" FROM "character" WHERE LOWER("character") IN ('a', 'b')"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character" FROM "character" WHERE LOWER("character") IN ('a', 'b')"#
);
```

#### pub fn [cust_with_values](https://docs.rs#method.cust_with_values)<T, V, I>(s: T, v: I) -> Self

Express any custom expression with [ Value](https://docs.rs/value/enum.Value.html). Use this if your expression needs variables.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-7)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(Expr::col(Char::Id).eq(1))
    .and_where(Expr::cust_with_values("6 = ? * ?", [2, 3]))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE `id` = 1 AND (6 = 2 * 3)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "id" = 1 AND (6 = 2 * 3)"#
);
```
```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(Expr::col(Char::Id).eq(1))
    .and_where(Expr::cust_with_values("6 = $2 * $1", [3, 2]))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "id" = 1 AND (6 = 2 * 3)"#
);
```
```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .expr(Expr::cust_with_values("6 = ? * ?", [2, 3]))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder), r#"SELECT 6 = 2 * 3"#);
assert_eq!(query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder), r#"SELECT 6 = 2 * 3"#);
```
Postgres only: use `$$` to escape `$`

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .expr(Expr::cust_with_values("$1 $$ $2", ["a", "b"]))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder), r#"SELECT 'a' $ 'b'"#);
```
```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .expr(Expr::cust_with_values("data @? ($1::JSONPATH)", ["hello"]))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT data @? ('hello'::JSONPATH)"#
);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sea_query/expr/enum.rs.html#493-499)#### pub fn [cust_with_expr](https://docs.rs#method.cust_with_expr)<T, E>(s: T, expr: E) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sea_query/expr/enum.rs.html#493-499)

#### pub fn [cust_with_expr](https://docs.rs#method.cust_with_expr)<T, E>(s: T, expr: E) -> Self

Express any custom expression with [ Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html). Use this if your expression needs other expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .expr(Expr::val(1).add(2))
    .expr(Expr::cust_with_expr("data @? ($1::JSONPATH)", "hello"))
    .to_owned();
let (sql, values) = query.build(PostgresQueryBuilder);
assert_eq!(sql, r#"SELECT $1 + $2, data @? ($3::JSONPATH)"#);
assert_eq!(
    values,
    Values(vec![1i32.into(), 2i32.into(), "hello".into()])
);
```

        "json_agg(DISTINCT $1)",
        Expr::col(Char::Character),
    ))
    .to_owned();

use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};

    .expr_as(Expr::exists(Query::select().column(Char::Id).from(Char::Table).take()), "character_exists")

);

#### pub fn [case](https://docs.rs#method.case)<C, T>(cond: C, then: T) -> [CaseStatement](https://docs.rs/query/struct.CaseStatement.html)

Adds new `CASE WHEN` to existing case statement.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .expr_as(
        Expr::case(
                Expr::col((Glyph::Table, Glyph::Aspect)).is_in([2, 4]),
                true
             )
            .finally(false),
         "is_even"
    )
    .from(Glyph::Table)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT (CASE WHEN ("glyph"."aspect" IN (2, 4)) THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END) AS "is_even" FROM "glyph""#
);
```

}## Expand description

“Operator” methods for building expressions.

Before `sea_query` 0.32.0 (`sea_orm` 1.1.1),
these methods were awailable only on [ Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)/

[and you needed to manually construct these types first.](https://docs.rs/type.SimpleExpr.html)

`SimpleExpr`Now, you can call them directly on any expression type:

```
let expr = 1_i32.cast_as("REAL");
let expr = Func::char_length("abc").eq(3_i32);
let expr = Expr::current_date().cast_as("TEXT").like("2024%");
```
If some methods are missing, look into [ BinOper::Custom](https://docs.rs/types/enum.BinOper.html#variant.Custom),

[, or](https://docs.rs/func/enum.Func.html#method.cust)

`Func::cust`[as a workaround, and consider reporting your issue.](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html#method.cust_with_values)

`Expr::cust*`## Required Methods[§](https://docs.rs#required-methods)

Express a `AS enum` expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::insert()
    .into_table(Char::Table)
    .columns([Char::FontSize])
    .values_panic(["large".as_enum("FontSizeEnum")])
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO `character` (`font_size`) VALUES ('large')"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "character" ("font_size") VALUES (CAST('large' AS "FontSizeEnum"))"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"INSERT INTO "character" ("font_size") VALUES ('large')"#
);
let query = Query::select()
    .expr(Expr::col(Char::FontSize).as_enum("FontSizeEnum[]"))
    .from(Char::Table)
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT CAST("font_size" AS "FontSizeEnum"[]) FROM "character""#
);
```
Create any binary operation

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .cond_where(all![
        Char::SizeW.into_column_ref().binary(BinOper::SmallerThan, 10),
        Char::SizeW.into_column_ref().binary(BinOper::GreaterThan, Char::SizeH.into_column_ref())
    ])
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE `size_w` < 10 AND `size_w` > `size_h`"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" < 10 AND "size_w" > "size_h""#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" < 10 AND "size_w" > "size_h""#
);
```

Express a logical `AND` operation.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .cond_where(any![
        Expr::col(Char::SizeW).eq(1).and(Expr::col(Char::SizeH).eq(2)),
        Expr::col(Char::SizeW).eq(3).and(Expr::col(Char::SizeH).eq(4)),
    ])
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE (`size_w` = 1 AND `size_h` = 2) OR (`size_w` = 3 AND `size_h` = 4)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE ("size_w" = 1 AND "size_h" = 2) OR ("size_w" = 3 AND "size_h" = 4)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE ("size_w" = 1 AND "size_h" = 2) OR ("size_w" = 3 AND "size_h" = 4)"#
);
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/sea_query/expr/trait.rs.html#500-502)

#### fn [in_subquery](https://docs.rs#method.in_subquery)(self, sel: [SelectStatement](https://docs.rs/query/struct.SelectStatement.html)) -> [Expr](https://docs.rs/enum.Expr.html)

Express a `IN` sub-query expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-19)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::SizeW, Char::SizeH])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(Char::SizeW.into_column_ref().in_subquery(
        Query::select()
            .expr(Expr::cust("3 + 2 * 2"))
            .take()
    ))
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE `size_w` IN (SELECT 3 + 2 * 2)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" IN (SELECT 3 + 2 * 2)"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE "size_w" IN (SELECT 3 + 2 * 2)"#
);
```
Express a `IN` sub expression.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-20)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Character, Char::FontId])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(
        Expr::tuple([
            Expr::col(Char::Character).into(),
            Expr::col(Char::FontId).into(),
        ]).in_tuples([(1, String::from("1")), (2, String::from("2"))])
    )
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `font_id` FROM `character` WHERE (`character`, `font_id`) IN ((1, '1'), (2, '2'))"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "font_id" FROM "character" WHERE ("character", "font_id") IN ((1, '1'), (2, '2'))"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "font_id" FROM "character" WHERE ("character", "font_id") IN ((1, '1'), (2, '2'))"#

);
```
The same query can be constructed using the `raw_query!` macro.

```
use sea_query::Values;
let ids: Vec<i32> = vec![1, 2, 3];
let query = sea_query::raw_query!(
    SqliteQueryBuilder,
    r#"SELECT "id" FROM "character" WHERE "character"."size_w" IN ({..ids})"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.sql,
    r#"SELECT "id" FROM "character" WHERE "character"."size_w" IN (?, ?, ?)"#
);
assert_eq!(query.values, Values(vec![1.into(), 2.into(), 3.into()]));
```
Empty value list is converted to an always false expression due to SQL syntax.

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .columns([Char::Id])
    .from(Char::Table)
    .and_where(
        (Char::Table, Char::SizeW)
            .into_column_ref()
            .is_in(Vec::<u8>::new()),
    )
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `id` FROM `character` WHERE 1 = 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "id" FROM "character" WHERE 1 = 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "id" FROM "character" WHERE 1 = 2"#
);
```

    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `character`, `size_w`, `size_h` FROM `character` WHERE 1 - 1 = 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(PostgresQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE 1 - 1 = 2"#
);
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(SqliteQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT "character", "size_w", "size_h" FROM "character" WHERE 1 - 1 = 2"#
);
```

Add an optional condition to the set.

Shorthand for `if o.is_some() { self.add(o) }`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use sea_query::{tests_cfg::*, *};
let query = Query::select()
    .column(Glyph::Image)
    .from(Glyph::Table)
    .cond_where(
        Cond::all()
            .add_option(Some(Expr::col((Glyph::Table, Glyph::Image)).like("A%")))
            .add_option(None::<Expr>),
    )
    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),
    r#"SELECT `image` FROM `glyph` WHERE `glyph`.`image` LIKE 'A%'"#
);
```
Create a condition that is true if any of the conditions is true.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use sea_query::{*, tests_cfg::*};
let query = Query::select()
    .column(Glyph::Image)
    .from(Glyph::Table)
    .cond_where(
        Cond::any()
            .add(Expr::col((Glyph::Table, Glyph::Aspect)).is_in([3, 4]))
            .add(Expr::col((Glyph::Table, Glyph::Image)).like("A%"))

    .to_owned();
assert_eq!(
    query.to_string(MysqlQueryBuilder),

);
