    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```

    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```

    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "1.0.0-rc.1"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive`

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`, `postgres-vector`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] constructors and [`ExprTrait`] methods
to construct `SELECT`, `JOIN`, `WHERE` and `HAVING` expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```
let table = truncate.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```
let index = create
    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```
let index = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

### Expression

Use [`Expr`] constructors and [`ExprTrait`] methods
to construct `SELECT`, `JOIN`, `WHERE` and `HAVING` expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

let query = select
    .column
    .column

    .to_owned;

    .to_owned;

# sea-query 0.32.7 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.32.7

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`, `postgres-vector`

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass).

# sea-query 0.32.4 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.32.4

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`, `postgres-vector`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] constructors and [`ExprTrait`] methods
to construct `SELECT`, `JOIN`, `WHERE` and `HAVING` expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```

    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```

    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```

    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```

    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;

assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```

    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;

### Index Drop

    .name

# sea-query 0.32.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.32.1

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```
let table = truncate.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```
let index = create
    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```
let index = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

# sea-query 0.32.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.32.0

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value

### Expression

### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```

```

```

```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

# sea-query 0.31.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.31.1

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

- Dynamic query

```

    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```

# sea-query 0.31.0-rc.8 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.31.0-rc.8

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;

    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```

    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;

```
### Foreign Key Create

    .name
    .from
    .to

    .on_update
    .to_owned;

```

let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to

    .on_update
    .to_owned;

// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```

    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;

// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables

    .to_owned;

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```

    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;

```

```

[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```
let table = truncate.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```
let index = create
    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```
let index = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

# sea-query 0.31.0-rc.1 - Docs.rs

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

### Condition

```

```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

# sea-query 0.30.5 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.30.5

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

# sea-query 0.30.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.30.2

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;

    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```

    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

```

    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;

### Foreign Key Create

    .name
    .from
    .to

# sea-query 0.29.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.29.1

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional (except `inherent`).

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```
let table = truncate.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```
let index = create
    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```
let index = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Advanced
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Aggregate Functions

`max`, `min`, `sum`, `avg`, `count` etc

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .from
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Casting

```
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Custom Function

```
;
let query = select
    .expr
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```
let table = truncate.table.to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support the TRUNCATE statement
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
let foreign_key = create
    .name
    .from
    .to
    .on_delete
    .on_update
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Foreign Key Drop

```
let foreign_key = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
// Sqlite does not support modification of foreign key constraints to existing tables
```
### Index Create

```
let index = create
    .name
    .table
    .col
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Index Drop

```
let index = drop
    .name
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```

# sea-query 0.28.5 - Docs.rs

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

## SeaQuery

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

# Cargo.toml

 = "^0"

### Feature flags

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

Query Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```

# sea-query 0.27.2 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.27.2

## Introduction

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "^0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional.

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL engine: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`with-ipnetwork`, `with-mac_address`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```

    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```

    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Foreign Key Create

    .to

    .on_update
    .to_owned;

```

    .name

# sea-query 0.26.3 - Docs.rs

## Introduction

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "^0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional.

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL dialect: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`postgres-array`

Driver support: `sqlx-mysql`, `sqlx-postgres`, `sqlx-sqlite`,
`postgres`, `postgres-*`, `rusqlite`

Postgres support: `postgres`, `postgres-chrono`, `postgres-json`, `postgres-rust_decimal`,
`postgres-bigdecimal`, `postgres-uuid`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

# sea-query 0.26.0 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/sea-query/0.26.0

## Introduction

SeaQuery is a query builder to help you construct dynamic SQL queries in Rust. You can construct expressions, queries and schema as abstract syntax trees using an ergonomic API. We support MySQL, Postgres and SQLite behind a common interface that aligns their behaviour where appropriate.

We provide integration for [SQLx](https://crates.io/crates/sqlx),
[postgres](https://crates.io/crates/postgres) and [rusqlite](https://crates.io/crates/rusqlite).
See [examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/blob/master/examples) for usage.

SeaQuery is the foundation of [SeaORM](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-orm), an async & dynamic ORM for Rust.

[
If you like what we do, consider starring, commenting, sharing and contributing!](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/stargazers/)

[
Join our Discord server to chat with others in the SeaQL community!](https://discord.com/invite/uCPdDXzbdv)

## Install

```
# Cargo.toml
[]
 = "^0"
```
SeaQuery is very lightweight, all dependencies are optional.

### Feature flags

Macro: `derive` `attr`

Async support: `thread-safe` (use `Arc` inplace of `Rc`)

SQL dialect: `backend-mysql`, `backend-postgres`, `backend-sqlite`

Type support: `with-chrono`, `with-time`, `with-json`, `with-rust_decimal`, `with-bigdecimal`, `with-uuid`,
`postgres-array`

Driver support: `sqlx-mysql`, `sqlx-postgres`, `sqlx-sqlite`,
`postgres`, `postgres-*`, `rusqlite`

Postgres support: `postgres`, `postgres-chrono`, `postgres-json`, `postgres-rust_decimal`,
`postgres-bigdecimal`, `postgres-uuid`, `postgres-array`, `postgres-interval`

## Usage

Table of Content

-
Basics
-
Query Statement
-
Schema Statement

### Motivation

Why would you want to use a dynamic query builder?

- Parameter bindings

One of the headaches when using raw SQL is parameter binding. With SeaQuery you can:

```
assert_eq!;
```
- Dynamic query

You can construct the query at runtime based on user inputs:

```
select
    .column
    .from
    .conditions;
```
### Iden

`Iden` is a trait for identifiers used in any query statement.

Commonly implemented by Enum where each Enum represents a table found in a database, and its variants include table name and column name.

[`Iden::unquoted()`] must be implemented to provide a mapping between Enum variants and its
corresponding string value.

```
use *;
// For example Character table with column id, character, font_size...
// Mapping between Enum variant and its corresponding string value
```
If you're okay with running another procedural macro, you can activate
the `derive` or `attr` feature on the crate to save you some boilerplate.
For more usage information, look at
[the derive examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-derive/tests/pass)
or [the attribute examples](https://github.com/SeaQL/sea-query/tree/master/sea-query-attr/tests/pass).

```
use Iden;
// This will implement Iden exactly as shown above
assert_eq!;
// You can also derive a unit struct
;
assert_eq!;
```
```
use ;
// It generates the following along with Iden impl
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Expression

Use [`Expr`] to construct select, join, where and having expression in query.

```
assert_eq!;
```
### Condition

If you have complex conditions to express, you can use the [`Condition`] builder,
usable for [`ConditionalStatement::cond_where`] and [`SelectStatement::cond_having`].

```
assert_eq!;
```
There is also the [`any!`] and [`all!`] macro at your convenience:

```
select.cond_where;
```
### Statement Builders

Statements are divided into 2 categories: Query and Schema, and to be serialized into SQL
with [`QueryStatementBuilder`] and [`SchemaStatementBuilder`] respectively.

Schema statement has the following interface:

```
;
```
Query statement has the following interfaces:

```
;
;
```
`build` builds a SQL statement as string and parameters to be passed to the database driver
through the binary protocol. This is the preferred way as it has less overhead and is more secure.

`to_string` builds a SQL statement as string with parameters injected. This is good for testing
and debugging.

### Query Select

```
let query = select
    .column
    .column
    .from
    .left_join
    .and_where
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Insert

```
let query = insert
    .into_table
    .columns
    .values_panic
    .values_panic
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Update

```
let query = update
    .table
    .values
    .and_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Query Delete

```
let query = delete
    .from_table
    .cond_where
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Create

```
let table = create
    .table
    .if_not_exists
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .col
    .foreign_key
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Alter

```
let table = alter
    .table
    .add_column
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Drop

```
let table = drop
    .table
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Rename

```
let table = rename
    .table
    .to_owned;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Table Truncate

```

assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
assert_eq!;
```
### Foreign Key Create

```
